title: Jarasandha Hurls His Mace toward Mathura
one_line_summary: Enraged by Kansa's death, Jarasandha whirls a mace ninety-nine times and hurls it toward Mathura where Krishna lives; the citizens inform Krishna of its fall.
source_excerpt: Some time after when king Kansa was slain by Vasudeva, an enmity arose between him and Krishna. Then, O Bharata, the mighty king of Magadha from his city of Girivraja, whirling a mace ninety-nine times, hurled it towards Mathura. At that time Krishna of wonderful deeds was residing at Mathura. ... The citizens beholding the circumstance well, went unto Krishna and informed him of the fall of the mace.
notes: Krishna narrates this backstory to Yudhishthira; the enmity is framed as the origin of the Jarasandha conflict.

title: Krishna Proposes Slaying Jarasandha as Prelude to the Rajasuya
one_line_summary: Krishna counsels that Jarasandha, unbeatable in battle by gods and asuras, must be slain in a bare-armed personal struggle, assigning policy to himself, strength to Bhima, and triumph to Arjuna.
source_excerpt: In me is policy, in Bhima is strength and in Arjuna is triumph; and therefore, as prelude to performing the Rajasuya, we will certainly achieve the destruction of the ruler of Magadha.
variant_notes: VARIANT of the Rajasuya slaying-plan: Mahabharata attributes the proposal to Krishna himself; Bhagavata Purana 10.71 presents the same plan as Uddhava's counsel to Krishna. Attribution difference is material — kept as separate stories.
notes: Krishna argues Jarasandha 'should be vanquished in a personal struggle with bare arms.'

title: Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna Set Out for Magadha in Disguise
one_line_summary: With Yudhishthira's blessing, Krishna, Arjuna and Bhima set out for Magadha attired as Snataka Brahmanas to confront Jarasandha.
source_excerpt: the trio Krishna, Arjuna and Bhima, all possessed of great energy, set out for Magadha attired in the garb of Snataka Brahmanas of resplendent bodies, and blessed by the agreeable speeches of friends and relatives.

title: Krishna and the Pandavas Break the Chaityaka Peak
one_line_summary: Entering Girivraja not by the gate but by piercing the sacred Chaityaka peak, Krishna, Bhima and Arjuna break down the celebrated hill worshipped by the Magadhas.
source_excerpt: On arriving then at the gate of the city, the brothers (instead of passing through it) began to pierce (with their shafts) the heart of the high Chaityaka peak that was worshipped by the race of Vrihadratha ... And attacking with their mighty arms that immovable and huge and high and old and celebrated peak always worshipped with perfumes and floral wreaths, those heroes broke it down.

title: Krishna Speaks for the Silent Disguised Brothers
one_line_summary: Received by Jarasandha, Krishna explains that his two companions observe a vow of silence until midnight, so he alone speaks for the disguised trio.
source_excerpt: And addressing the monarch Krishna said,--'O king of kings these two are now in the observance of a vow. Therefore they will not speak. Silent they will remain till midnight After that hour they will speak with thee!'

title: Krishna Answers Jarasandha's Challenge about the Disguise
one_line_summary: When Jarasandha censures the disguised guests for entering by an improper gate, Krishna replies that a foe's abode is entered by the wrong gate and the foe's hospitality is refused.
source_excerpt: These are the rules of the ordinance, viz., that an enemy's abode should be entered through a wrong gate and a friend's abode through the right one. And know, O monarch, that this also is our eternal vow that having entered the foe's abode for the accomplishment of our purpose, we accept not the worship offered to us!

title: Krishna Reveals Their Identities and Challenges Jarasandha
one_line_summary: Krishna casts off the Brahmana disguise, declares himself Sauri and his companions the sons of Pandu, and challenges Jarasandha to free the captive kings or fight.
source_excerpt: Desirous of liberating the captive monarchs from thee, know that we are certainly not Brahmanas. I am Hrishesha otherwise called Sauri, and these two heroes among men are the sons of Pandu. O king of Magadha, we challenge thee. Fight standing before us. Either set free all the monarchs, or go thou to the abode of Yama.

title: Krishna Refrains from Slaying Jarasandha
one_line_summary: Remembering Brahma's command that Jarasandha is destined to die at Bhima's hands, Krishna withholds his own hand and leaves the king to Bhima.
source_excerpt: the lord Sauri ever devoted to truth ... keeping in view the command of Brahma and remembering that the ruler of Magadha was destined to be slain in battle by Bhima and not by the descendant of Madhu (Yadavas), desired not to slay himself king Jarasandha.
notes: The actual wrestling match and slaying fall in sections beyond the assigned range.

title: Krishna Arrives at Indraprastha with Treasure
one_line_summary: Krishna, appointing Vasudeva to command the Yadava army, arrives at Khandava with a vast mass of treasure to support Yudhishthira's sacrifice.
source_excerpt: Hari (Krishna) ... having appointed Vasudeva to the command of the (Yadava) army, and bringing with him for the king Yudhishthira just a large mass of treasure; entered that excellent city of cities. Khandava, himself surrounded by a mighty host and filling the atmosphere with the rattle of his chariot-wheels.

title: Krishna Grants Permission for the Rajasuya
one_line_summary: When Yudhishthira asks leave to perform the Rajasuya, Krishna praises his virtues and sanctions the great sacrifice.
source_excerpt: Krishna, extolling his virtues, said.--'Thou, O tiger among kings, deservest imperial dignity. Let, therefore, the great sacrifice be performed by thee. And if thou performest that sacrifice an obtainest its fruit we all shall regard ourselves as crowned with success.'

title: Krishna Washes the Feet of the Brahmanas
one_line_summary: At the Rajasuya, Krishna the lord of all worlds humbly takes up the menial office of washing the feet of the Brahmanas.
source_excerpt: Krishna who was himself the centre of all worlds and round whom moved every creature, desirous of acquiring excellent fruits, was engaged at his own will in washing the feet of the Brahmanas.

title: Bhishma Declares Krishna Foremost and He Receives the First Arghya
one_line_summary: Judging Krishna foremost among all present, Bhishma directs that he receive the first Arghya; Sahadeva presents it and Krishna accepts it, kindling Shishupala's fury.
source_excerpt: Bhishma the son of Santanu, judged it by his intelligence that on earth Krishna was the foremost of all. ... Sahadeva endued with great prowess duly presented the first Arghya of excellent ingredients unto Krishna of the Vrishni race. Krishna also accepted it according to the forms of the ordinance. But Sisupala could not bear to see that worship offered unto Vasudeva.

title: Shishupala Reviles Krishna and Storms Out of the Assembly
one_line_summary: Shishupala denounces the worship of Krishna as unworthy, reviles Bhishma and Yudhishthira, and walks out of the assembly with the kings.
source_excerpt: This wretch born in the race of the Vrishnis unrighteously slew of old the illustrious king Jarasandha. ... Having spoken these words, Sisupala rose from his excellent seat, and accompanied by the kings, went out of that assembly.

title: Shishupala Incites the Kings to Battle
one_line_summary: Shishupala rallies the angry monarchs to obstruct the sacrifice, and Krishna perceives that the assembled kings are preparing for a rush.
source_excerpt: Upon Krishna having received the first worship, Sunitha (Sisupala) ... said,--'When I am here to head ye all, what are ye thinking of now? Arrayed let us stand in battle against the assembled Vrishnis and the Pandavas?' ... Krishna then understood that the vast sea of monarchs with its countless waves of troops was preparing for a terrific rush.

title: Bhishma Foretells That Krishna Will Destroy Shishupala
one_line_summary: As Yudhishthira fears for his sacrifice, Bhishma declares the kings mere barking dogs before the sleeping lion of the Vrishnis, and that Vishnu has resolved to take back Shishupala's energy.
source_excerpt: As dogs in a pack approaching the lion that is asleep bark together, so are all these lords of earth. ... Assuredly, O Bharata Vishnu hath been desirous of taking back unto himself the energy that existeth in this Sisupala.

title: Shishupala Derides Krishna's Deeds and Bhima's Wrath Is Restrained
one_line_summary: Shishupala scoffs at Krishna's childhood feats (the slaying of Putana, the lifting of Govardhan, the slaying of Kansa), enraging Bhima until Bhishma restrains him.
source_excerpt: If Krishna in his infancy slew a vulture, what is there remarkable in that ... O Bhishma, what is there remarkable in this one's having supported for a week the Govardhan mount which is like an anthill? ... Bhimasena endued with energy became angry. ... the mighty-armed Bhishma caught him like Mahadeva seizing Mahasena.
notes: Shishupala's taunts rehearse Krishna's Vrindavan-era feats in derision.

title: Krishna Fulfils the Prophecy over Infant Shishupala
one_line_summary: When Shishupala is born with three eyes and four arms, Krishna, on a visit to Chedi, takes the infant on his lap; the extra arms fall away and the third eye vanishes, marking Krishna as the destined slayer.
source_excerpt: the queen with great pleasure herself placed the child on the lap of Damodara. As soon as the child was placed on his lap, those superfluous arms of his fell down and the eye on his forehead also disappeared.
notes: Narrated by Bhishma as backstory within the assembly.

title: Krishna Grants Shishupala's Mother the Boon of a Hundred Offences
one_line_summary: When the frightened queen begs a boon, Krishna promises to pardon a hundred offences of Shishupala for her sake, a promise that now nears its limit.
source_excerpt: Krishna then said, 'O aunt, even when he will deserve to be slain, I will pardon an hundred offences of his. Grieve thou not.'
notes: This boon frames the eventual slaying, which falls beyond the assigned sections.

title: Draupadi Invokes Krishna as She Is Dragged and Disrobed
one_line_summary: As Dussasana drags her before the assembly and strips her, Draupadi cries out to Govinda, Kesava and Janarddana to rescue her from the Kaurava ocean.
source_excerpt: 'O Govinda, O thou who dwellest in Dwaraka, O Krishna, O thou who art fond of cow-herdesses (of Vrindavana). O Kesava, seest thou not that the Kauravas are humiliating me. O Lord, O husband of Lakshmi, O Lord of Vraja (Vrindavana), O destroyer of all afflictions, O Janarddana, rescue me who am sinking in the Kaurava Ocean.'

title: Krishna Protects Draupadi with Endless Robes
one_line_summary: Moved by Draupadi's call, Krishna comes to her aid from compassion; the unseen Dharma covers her so that as each garment is dragged off another appears, hundreds of robes protecting her honour.
source_excerpt: Hearing the words of Draupadi, Krishna was deeply moved. And leaving his seat, the benevolent one from compassion, arrived there on foot. ... the illustrious Dharma, remaining unseen, covered her with excellent clothes of many hues. And, O monarch as the attire of Draupadi was being dragged, after one was taken off, another of the same kind, appeared covering her. ... owing to the protection of Dharma, hundreds upon hundreds of robes of many hues came off Draupadi's person.
notes: The miracle of the inexhaustible garment; in Ganguli the protection is attributed to 'the illustrious Dharma' responding to Krishna's compassion.

title: Krishna Vows the Earth Shall Drink the Blood of the Pandavas' Foes
one_line_summary: Visiting the exiled Pandavas in the forest, an enraged Krishna vows that the earth shall drink the blood of Duryodhana, Karna, Dussasana and Sakuni, and that Yudhishthira will be reinstalled on the throne.
source_excerpt: Kesava mournfully said, 'The earth shall drink the blood of Duryodhana and Karna, of Dussasana and the wicked Sakuni! Slaying these in battle and defeating their followers along with their royal allies, will we all install Yudhishthira the just on the throne! The wicked deserve to be slain! Verily, this is eternal morality.'

title: Arjuna Pacifies the Wrathful Krishna
one_line_summary: When Krishna, inflamed by the Pandavas' wrongs, seems bent on consuming all creatures, Arjuna recites his former divine feats to calm him, and Krishna answers that he and Arjuna are Nara and Narayana.
source_excerpt: when on account of the wrongs of Pritha's sons, Janardana had thus got into a passion, and seemed bent upon consuming all created things, Arjuna exerted himself to pacify him. ... 'Thou art mine and I am thine, while all that is mine is thine also! ... O thou irrepressible one, thou art Nara and I am Narayana or Hari!'
notes: Arjuna's long recitation of Krishna's former feats is discourse; the beat here is Krishna's consuming wrath and its pacification.

title: Krishna Promises Draupadi She Will Be Queen Again
one_line_summary: To the weeping Draupadi, Krishna vows that the wives of her enemies shall weep over their slain husbands and that she will once more be queen of kings, his words never futile.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva then spake unto the weeping Draupadi as follows, 'O fair lady, the wives of those with whom thou art angry, shall weep even like thee, beholding their husbands dead on the ground, weltering in blood ... I promise thou shalt (once more) be the queen of kings! The heavens might fall, or the Himavat might split, the earth might be rent, or the waters of the ocean might dry up, but my words shall never be futile!'

title: Krishna Laments His Absence from the Dice Game
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Yudhishthira that had he been present at Dwarka he would have prevented the dice game by counsel or force, and that his absence while fighting Salwa caused the Pandavas' calamity.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, O lord of earth, if I had been present at Dwaraka, then, O king, this evil would not have befallen thee! ... O Kauravya, it is owing to my absence from the Anartta country at that time that thou hast fallen into such distress begot of dice!
notes: This frames the Salwa/Saubha narrative that follows in sections 21-23.

title: Krishna Swoons at Salwa's Illusion of His Father's Death
one_line_summary: During the battle with Salwa, a false messenger claims Salwa has slain Vasudeva; seeing the vision of his father falling, Krishna swoons and drops his Sharanga bow, only later concluding it was illusion.
source_excerpt: And now I saw, O great monarch, Vasudeva himself falling from the car of precious metals! And, O warrior I swooned away ... Then the bow Sharanga dropped from my hand, and, O son of Kunti I swooned away! ... Then I concluded in my mind that it was certainly illusion.
notes: Krishna narrates this Dwaraka-period battle (the Saubha/Salwa episode) to Yudhishthira. Event occurred in Krishna's Dwaraka period, though narrated during the Pandava exile.

title: Krishna Shatters the Rock-Shower with Indra's Thunderbolt
one_line_summary: Buried under torrents of rocks hurled by Salwa's Danavas, Krishna wields Indra's thunderbolt and destroys the entire mass of crags, then resumes the fight.
source_excerpt: torrents of rocks falling upon me covered me up, and I began to grow like an ant-hill ... And then wielding the thunderbolt, that favourite (weapon) of Indra, capable of riving stones, I destroyed that entire mass of crags!
notes: Part of Krishna's retrospective narration of the Saubha/Salwa battle.

title: Krishna Destroys the Flying City of Saubha
one_line_summary: Launching the Sudarsana discus, Krishna cuts the aerial city of Saubha in twain so that it falls like Tripura shaken by Mahadeva's shafts.
source_excerpt: And approaching the town of Saubha whose splendour had disappeared, the discus went right through it, even as a saw divideth a tall tree. And cut in twain by the energy of the Sudarsana it fell like the city of Tripura shaken by the shafts of Maheswara.
notes: The Sudarsana discus is named explicitly here.

title: Krishna Slays Salwa with the Sudarsana Discus
one_line_summary: Retaking the discus, Krishna hurls it at Salwa, cleaving him in twain as he is about to hurl his mace, and setting the foe ablaze.
source_excerpt: And taking it up I once more hurled it with force saying, 'Go thou unto Salwa.' The discus then cleft Salwa in twain who in that fierce conflict was at the point of hurling a heavy mace. And with its energy it set the foe ablaze.
